supersession_note: Version 1.1 separates raw EnvBench Official outcomes from run qualification and failure attribution. It also narrows the R1 and cumulative-progress claims.

raw_official_outcomes.authority: Raw postepisode EnvBench Official results are reported independently of qualification and causal attribution.

raw_nonpasses.attribution: PyPI SSL EOF observed during package acquisition

raw_official_outcomes.interpretation: P has the best raw table in this sequential screen. This is not yet a causal reliability result: at position 22 P changed from conda to system Python plus venv, while R0 and R1 retained conda, and the arms ran at different times. The acquisition failure may therefore be deployment-policy-mediated, time-varying network behavior, or both. D2 is controlled development evidence, not a leaderboard result.

R1.note: Position 23 D2 remains a raw Official Pass even though its run audit is invalid. Position 22 D2 remains a raw Official nonpass even though its run audit is invalid.

qualification_and_protocol.principle: Audit validity determines whether a cell supports mechanism attribution; it does not rewrite the raw Official score.

model_usage.accounting: All available model usage from scheduled arm executions is retained. Controller-only attempts and zero-model retries add no model tokens. Two interrupted Agent attempts have unavailable usage and are reported separately.

comparisons.interpretation: P versus R0 is a mixed tradeoff: P used 6.6% more total input and 12.6% more output, but 14.0% less uncached input. The four projects, not the eight conditions, are the independent units. No dominance or noninferiority claim is supported.

model_usage.R1_confound: R1 always forked the completed session and requested improvement, whereas P and R0 skipped the model after a passing replay. The 58.5% P-versus-R1 input reduction therefore mixes trigger policy with memory representation. It only supports a claim about this always-call full-history policy.

cumulative_progress_gap.planned_test: Compare D0, D1, and D2 state versions on the same fixed condition Q without updating state during probes.
cumulative_progress_gap.available_artifacts: Four v1 seeds and 24 v2/v3 runtime state files exist.
cumulative_progress_gap.missing_evidence: No state-version by fixed-Q probe matrix was executed. The current study is a sequential reuse-and-repair screen, not a completed cumulative-progress experiment.
cumulative_progress_gap.state_persistence_issue: R1 v3 for positions 17 and 23 still records D1, and position 22 still records D0, despite D2 execution. Submitted program artifacts must therefore be treated as authoritative for any supplement; state-file persistence failures are retained as method cost.

findings.finding: The current explicit-state candidate P is not ready for promotion.
findings.evidence: It has the best raw Official table, but the position-22 advantage is causally ambiguous, costs trade off across token categories, and the planned fixed-Q cumulative-progress test is missing.

findings.finding: Always-call full-session improvement is expensive in this screen.
findings.evidence: R1 used 2.57 times R0 total input while changing both trigger policy and memory representation.
findings.scope: This does not reject adaptive full-history reuse after a failed replay.

findings.finding: Ordinary executable-program reuse is a strong simple comparator, not a proven optimum.
findings.evidence: R0 frequently skipped model work after successful replay, but it did not receive the same information as P and had two raw Official nonpasses.

strongest_alternative_explanations: P's raw advantage at position 22 may come from its venv deployment choice rather than explicit state itself.
Sequential execution and time-varying package acquisition may explain some arm differences.
R1's cost may come from always requesting improvement rather than from full history.
The successful executable program may already contain nearly all reusable benefit; the additional state may add little.

stage_decision.reason: The claimed mechanism gain is unestablished; this does not show that explicit state is useless or that R0 is optimal.

minimum_supplement_proposal.projects: the same four consumed/Dev projects; no replacement
minimum_supplement_proposal.question: Does the repaired submitted program reduce repeated deployment failure enough to justify its update cost, or has the previously successful program already absorbed all reusable benefit?
minimum_supplement_proposal.design: On each predeclared D2 condition, interleave repeated zero-model clean replays of the exact pre-update v2 program and exact post-update submitted program for P and R0. Do not update state. Use a fixed order declared before execution and report raw success, acquisition signature, replay wall time, and the already-incurred D2 update tokens/wall time separately.
minimum_supplement_proposal.primary_readout: Repeated clean-replay success on fixed D2 Q, summarized by four independent projects.
minimum_supplement_proposal.secondary_readout: Amortization of update cost over later successful replays; no claim if programs have equal repeated success.
minimum_supplement_proposal.why_this_first: It directly tests whether repair creates reusable progress using existing artifacts, without new model calls, new projects, new rules, or protected data.
